current_bottleneck: The 287c/287d/287e bracket shows that query-key design alone is no longer the main bottleneck. A mixed fast-local / slow-global query key can recover aggregate structure and local fidelity together, but the single-nearest deterministic retrieval still cannot activate the right strong mean-reverting cells while keeping the time-series tail shape in gate. The likely cap is now the single-neighbor support use, not the embedding choice.
last_result_summary: Iteration 115 ran 287e-v0 and got 4/11. It confirmed the mixed-query hypothesis: aggregate MR recovered from 0.168 to 0.928, active-cell slope correlation recovered to 0.731, and change KS reached 25/25 while level KS stayed above 287c. But active-pass rate collapsed to 8.3% and the score stayed at 4/11. This closes the local query-key sub-branch as locally exhausted.
next_step_recommendation: Run post-experiment analysis over 287c/287d/287e, then choose the next smallest Stage A move. The leading hypothesis is a deterministic top-k or soft retrieval replay that keeps the 287e mixed query key but changes the single-nearest support use.
current_best_model: 277d-v0, 279a-v0, 281a-v0, 281b-v0, and 282b-v0 are the current overall co-frontiers at 5/11 in the two-level reset.
current_best_note: 282b is still the cleanest current Stage B objective frontier at 5/11, but 284b and 285a strengthen the conclusion that the real cap is now the Stage A support object rather than the Stage B weighting law.
